record.paper_title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems
record.original_question: When recursive types interact with channel or reference constructors in semantic subtyping, some natural recursive extensions appear to admit no model. What exactly does the non-existence of a model signify: a limitation of the semantic-subtyping methodology, or a deeper semantic obstruction inherent to those type constructors? More generally, can one characterize when recursive extensions of a semantically defined type system will or will not admit a model?

evidence.quote: This raises the problem to understand what the non-existence of a model means. Does it correspond to a limit of the semantic subtyping approach, a limit that some different approach could overcome, or does it instead characterise some mathematical properties of the semantics of the types, by reaching the limits that every semantic interpretation of these types cannot overcome?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the semantic-subtyping methodology, a type system is interpreted by fixing a set-theoretic model: types are interpreted as subsets of some domain D in such a way that the type connectives (union, intersection, negation, product, arrow, and constructor symbols such as reference types ref(·) and channel types chan(·)) correspond to set-theoretic operations, and the subtyping relation t ≤ s is defined by the inclusion ⟦t⟧ ⊆ ⟦s⟧. Recursive types are admitted by allowing regular (possibly infinite) trees built from these connectives.

It is known that some natural recursive extensions of such systems admit no model in this sense. For example, when recursion is allowed to traverse a reference-type or channel-type constructor without restriction (i.e. without requiring that on every infinite branch of the regular type only finitely many occurrences of ref or chan appear), the resulting set-theoretic interpretation becomes inconsistent and no model exists.

Provide a precise mathematical answer to the following:

1. Characterize the meaning of the non-existence of a model in semantic subtyping when recursive types interact with invariant constructors such as ref(·) and chan(·). Specifically, determine whether this non-existence reflects:
   (a) a limitation intrinsic to the set-theoretic / semantic-subtyping methodology, which could be overcome by an alternative semantic framework yielding a sound and complete subtyping relation for the same type connectives; or
   (b) a genuine semantic obstruction, in the sense that no semantic interpretation respecting the intended algebraic laws of these constructors can exist.

2. More generally, give a characterization (necessary and sufficient conditions) on a semantically defined type system, equipped with a collection of type constructors and a recursion scheme on regular trees, that determines exactly when a recursive extension admits a model and when it does not.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and follow-up work on semantic subtyping confirm that the non-existence of models for recursion through reference/channel constructors is observed and worked around by syntactic restrictions (only finitely many ref/chan occurrences on each infinite branch), but no general characterization of when recursive extensions admit a model has been established. The conceptual question of whether this reflects a methodological limit or an inherent semantic obstruction remains open.

status_evidence.title: A Gentle Introduction to Semantic Subtyping
status_evidence.snippet: Restrictions are imposed on recursive types so that ref/chan constructors occur only finitely often along each infinite branch, because the natural unrestricted extension is inconsistent.
status_evidence.claim: The community uses syntactic restrictions to avoid model non-existence, but does not provide a general characterization.

status_evidence.title: Semantic subtyping: dealing set-theoretically with function, union, intersection, and negation types
status_evidence.snippet: Develops set-theoretic models for rich type connectives but treats invariant constructors with restrictions; general model-existence for recursive extensions is not characterized.
status_evidence.claim: No general criterion for model existence of recursive semantic-subtyping extensions is given.
